agent_note: First-person retrospective comic SF. All 23 event quotes are past; zero present event-narration. The book carries a very heavy load of narrator-present commentary addressed to the reader (habitual-present exposition about the setting, second-person jokes, science digressions) -- 31 of 78 quotes. Policy applied consistently: timeless/habitual present commentary that states how the story world or the real world generally works = gnomic (this is exactly the timeless-present contamination the bucket exists to catch); present tense about a specific character at a specific story-moment would have been event/present, but no quote met that test. Several rule-of-thumb gnomics generalize within the story world rather than beyond it (q01904, q01926, q01930) -- flagged in notes rather than decided silently. Dialogue calls rest on register/vocatives/direct address for the many quotes with quotation marks stripped; q01905, q01922 and q01940 are near-ties on word count and were kept in the non-diagnostic bucket. Prose, not verse. No single quote would flip the label.
